historical_flood_observations.evidence: IFI v3 entries since 2016: Kolkata 4, Mumbai 40 (event-level, district). OpenAlex works 'X AND flood': Kolkata 211, Mumbai 623; 'X AND waterlogging': Kolkata 25, Mumbai 11. Locality-level waterlogging reports verified in this run: Kolkata 93 localities / 14 dated events (accessible archive); Mumbai not verified in this run.
historical_flood_observations.note: Mumbai is clearly stronger at event level, Kolkata verified at locality level; scored equal in the base case (see sensitivity).

rainfall_observations.evidence: Both covered by IMD 0.25 deg gridded daily, ERA5 hourly, CHIRPS daily. Mumbai's strong orographic gradient makes 0.25 deg grids less representative; Kolkata's gridded product shows station-sampling artefacts (2025-09-23).

satellite_flood_extent.evidence: Sentinel-1 RTC monsoon (Jun-Oct) acquisitions 2017-2025: Kolkata 523 across 3 orbits, Mumbai 115 on essentially one orbit.
satellite_flood_extent.post_hoc: Later analysis in this run showed Sentinel-1 change detection carries no rainfall-driven signal in Kolkata's built-up cells, so this advantage did not translate into usable urban labels.

elevation_terrain.evidence: Copernicus GLO-30 relief (p95-p5): Kolkata 10.1 m, Mumbai 130.2 m. In Kolkata DSM errors are comparable to the terrain signal.

land_use.evidence: ESA WorldCover 2021 (10 m) and JRC GSW available for both.

drainage_infrastructure.evidence: OSM drain/ditch/canal ways: Kolkata 385, Mumbai 747. Neither city's storm-drain network is openly published.

population_exposure.evidence: GHS-POP for both; OSM building ways in study bbox: Kolkata 498,494, Mumbai 116,716; health/school features Kolkata 749, Mumbai 2290.

independent_validation.evidence: Kolkata: multi-orbit SAR, IFI, news archive. Mumbai: dense IFI record and larger literature for comparison.

decision: Kolkata selected as pilot. The primary deliverable is a within-city spatial susceptibility map, which needs locality-level observations; these were verified for Kolkata in this run. Totals are close and the ranking flips with reasonable changes to the historical-observation score or the post-hoc satellite score, so the choice is not robustly dominant. Mumbai has the stronger event-level record and is the recommended next city (especially for temporal event modelling).
approach: Neither city has openly available, systematically recorded, time-stamped urban flood labels at hourly resolution. The pilot therefore uses (A) presence/background susceptibility from documented localities and (B) city-scale documented event-day discrimination from rainfall, not hourly flood forecasting.
